doc.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Stockton, Pacific and the Army years
title: Integrated bands: the Wolf Pack and earlier mixed groups
summary: He claims he integrated the Army band and recalls earlier mixed groups, including the octet and a Modesto trio in 1939.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: While you were in the Army, you were part of a group known as the Wolf Pack. This was a racially integrated jazz band.
Had you worked with integrated bands before that?
Yeah. From the – even the octet in ’46 had a saxophonist from San Francisco. I’m ashamed to say at the moment I can’t remember his name. Iola would.
We can fill that in. We’re going to get the transcript, and we can add – we’re going to be able to edit the transcript of these things.
Then I played with mixed groups [ ] ’39.
In the Wagon Wheel in Modesto. It was just two guitar players. They asked me to play with then.
So there were three musicians playing.
